problems.description: 50 naming-convention violations across the new files (snake_case functions, non-PascalCase interfaces/classes, constants not UPPER_CASE) — the new code abandons the seed's established TypeScript conventions (measured convention score 0.51).
Cognitive complexity +18 and code smells +1 — the CLI argument parsing and generator logic are more convoluted than the task warrants.
SonarQube reports +1 new bug; the root cause is not visible in the truncated diff but represents a genuine correctness defect.
The 200-line seed (index.ts) was deleted wholesale and replaced rather than built upon; acceptable for a greenfield session but it discarded the existing baseline and its conventions without reuse.

strengths: On-task for the static_site_gen story: modular SSG layout (src/cli.ts bin entry, src/generator.ts, src/hash.ts, content -> dist) with appropriate dependencies (gray-matter, marked).
Test infrastructure established from session 1 (jest.config.js + --runInBand test script, tests/ roots).
commit_reviews.summary: A structurally sound, on-task SSG build that is nonetheless worse than the seed it replaced on raw quality — +1 bug, +1 smell, +18 cognitive complexity, 50 convention violations — with one discrepancy flagged: the AST reports +0 classes while SonarQube flags 'Classes should use PascalCase', indicating the class detection is heuristic.

problems.description: Hand-rolls two regex-based template engines (Handlebars + EJS) with partial/layout resolution instead of using an established library — fragile parsing of nested blocks, escaped braces, and whitespace, contributing +45 cognitive complexity and +141 lines to a small SSG that already depends on marked.

+6 new functions and two template dialects (renderHandlebars, renderEjs, createRenderer, templateFiles, find) are added with zero tests — no coverage for partial resolution, layout fallback, or the each/if/include constructs.
Truthiness-based {{#if}} evaluation renders valid falsey values (0, empty string) as absent, and @index is computed via items.indexOf giving O(n^2) behavior in each blocks.

Convention score 0.51 per measurement, but the listed violations (Classes/Interfaces PascalCase, snake_case functions, hash.ts flagged) are not introduced by this diff — hash.ts is untouched and the new code uses camelCase/PascalCase consistently, so the measurement appears dominated by pre-existing tooling noise.

strengths: Backward-compatible feature: --templates flag, optional template/layout Page fields, and buildSite default-param extension preserve existing behavior
Graceful degradation: missing templates dir (ENOENT) returns empty, and resolution falls back from custom template to default layout to raw body
Covers both Handlebars and EJS dialects with partial/include support, scoped to the SSG domain
commit_reviews.summary: Adds a legitimate templating feature with backward-compatible signatures, but implements it as hand-rolled regex engines with no tests, flagging +45 cognitive complexity that offsets the feature value at roughly a neutral architectural outcome.

problems.description: New server.ts module (dev server, HTTP serving, WebSocket live reload, file watching) ships with zero test coverage — startServer, serveFile, injectReload, and the rebuild-queue logic are all untested.
Hand-rolled rebuild serialization (rebuilding/queued flag pair) drives the measured +38 cognitive complexity and +2 smells; a small debounce helper would be simpler and testable.
chokidar and ws are only used by the serve/dev path but are placed in runtime dependencies rather than devDependencies.
Uses client.OPEN instance property instead of the WebSocket.OPEN static; reloadScript const is lowercase despite an UPPER_CASE constants rule existing in the repo's convention checker.
Reload-script regex scan and injection run on every HTML request; negligible for a dev server but could be cached per file.

strengths: Composes cleanly with the existing pipeline by reusing buildSite rather than duplicating generation logic.
Serve-time reload injection keeps the static build output pristine — no reload script leaks into dist/.
Path-traversal protection via path.resolve root containment check on served files.
Rebuild serialization prevents concurrent-build race conditions on rapid file events.
Minimal, consistent CLI extension (serve command + --port) matching the existing options() argument-parsing pattern.
commit_reviews.summary: A clean, well-composed integration commit that layers a live-reload dev server onto the existing generator with a proper public API seam and security-conscious file serving, held back only by its lack of tests and the +38 cognitive-complexity rebuild queue.

problems.description: Cache correctness: the skip path restores cached pages keyed by source hash, but readCache only validates version/shape and never compares the stored templateHash against a freshly computed one, so a template change can serve stale HTML (matches the SonarQube +1 bug delta).

Cognitive complexity +30 is concentrated in buildSiteWithStats; the skip/restore branch plus the cache-write loop and plugin pipeline should be extracted into smaller helpers (consistent with the +3 smells delta).
The .ssg-cache.json is written into the output directory (./dist), leaking build machinery into published output unless excluded by the deploy step.

DISCREPANCY: the mechanical convention score (0.51) is driven by violations that contradict the code — cli.ts has no classes, the interfaces (BuildOptions/BuildStats/BuildResult/BuildCache) ARE PascalCase, and all functions are camelCase — so the listed violations read as false positives from a misconfigured checker rather than real TS convention breaks.

strengths: Backward-compatible: buildSite is preserved as a thin wrapper over buildSiteWithStats, so existing callers and the public re-export in index.ts keep working unchanged.
Versioned cache format (version: 1) with per-source sha256 hashes and a clean() escape hatch provides a sane invalidation foundation for future work.
Solid TypeScript style: camelCase functions, PascalCase interfaces, explicit return types, node: built-in prefix, no any — qualitatively well above the mechanical 0.51 score.
Incremental stats (built/skipped/time saved) surfaced in CLI output and a dedicated BuildStats/BuildResult type — good observability for the cross-cutting session goal.
commit_reviews.summary: A well-shaped, backward-compatible incremental-build feature that fits the existing architecture, though it carries real complexity and a likely cache-staleness bug; the 0.51 convention score looks like a checker false positive since the flagged violations contradict the actual code style.

compounding_issues: No Node toolchain in the environment (npm/node/jest/tsc all 'command not found'), so every session's tests/builds failed to execute — runtime correctness is unverified and rests entirely on code inspection

Session 2's hand-rolled template engines (mini-Handlebars/mini-EJS) persisted unchanged and became the ceiling on template expressiveness for later sessions (no arbitrary-helper evaluation, limited loop semantics)
Small accumulated code smells from early sessions carried to the end: double gray-matter frontmatter parse in parseMarkdown and a redundant parseMarkdown import in generator.ts
The dev server (Session 3) and incremental cache (Session 5) were both integrated without any runtime verification, so their correctness depends on inspection of untested paths
key_decisions: Session 1 greenfield: discarded the unrelated auth-API seed entirely and scaffolded a clean strict-TS project (tsconfig strict, jest, src/ layout) rather than adapting the seed
Session 2: hand-rolled Handlebars AND EJS renderers with layouts/partials/template-frontmatter instead of pulling in handlebars/ejs packages — small dependency footprint, dual dialect support
Session 4: full plugin architecture over a shared BuildContext (MarkdownPlugin, TemplatePlugin, DevServerPlugin) — de-monolithized generator.ts and decoupled concerns before complexity compounded

Session 5: hash-based incremental build cache (source content-hash + template fingerprint invalidation) threaded through the plugin context as BuildState — a cross-cutting feature enabled by the Session 4 refactor
Session 3: dev-server integration with chokidar file watching + WebSocket live-reload and path-traversal protection in the static file server
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily across all five sessions. Session 1 produced a clean but simple two-test core; Session 2 meaningfully expanded capability with a custom dual-dialect template engine and layouts; Session 3 integrated a full watch+reload dev server; Session 4 was a disciplined, behavior-preserving refactor that turned the monolith into a plugin system; Session 5 added a genuinely sophisticated cross-cutting feature (content-hash + template-hash incremental caching with clean-build handling) while expanding tests from 4 to 6. The test suite grew from 2 to 6 tests and consistently targeted each new capability as it landed. The only persistent caveat is that no test could ever be executed (missing Node toolchain), so the consistently green-by-inspection suite was never actually run.
story_review.summary: A textbook, highly coherent software lifecycle arc (scaffold → feature → integrate → refactor → cross-cutting optimization) where each session built directly on the prior commit and quality and test coverage improved monotonically, though none of it was ever runtime-verified due to a missing Node toolchain.
